nodes.name: Spherical configuration space $S_N$ and surface measure $\lambda_N$
nodes.statement: For given $N\geq 1,$ we denote by $S_N=\{{\vec{\sigma}}\in\mathbb{R}^N:\|{\vec{\sigma}}\|=\sqrt{N}\}$ the configuration space and by $\lambda_N$ its normalized surface measure.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.

nodes.name: Pure $p$-spin Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: Consider the pure $p$-spin Hamiltonians $H_{N,p}({\vec{\sigma}})$ for $p\geq 1$ indexed by ${\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N,$ \begin{align} H_{N,p}({\vec{\sigma}})=\frac{1}{N^{(p-1)/2}}\sum_{1\leq i_1,\ldots,i_p\leq N}g_{i_1,\ldots,i_p}\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_p}, \end{align} where the random variables $g_{i_1,\ldots,i_p}$ for all $p\geq 1$ and all $(i_1,\ldots,i_p)$ are i.i.d. standard Gaussian.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.statement_short: Pure $p$-spin Hamiltonian on $S_N$: normalized sum of i.i.d. standard Gaussians times degree-$p$ spin monomials.

nodes.name: Pure p-spin Hamiltonian (1.1)
nodes.statement: H_{N,p}({\vec{\sigma}})=\frac{1}{N^{(p-1)/2}}\sum_{1\leq i_1,\ldots,i_p\leq N}g_{i_1,\ldots,i_p}\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_p},
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.label: eq1

nodes.name: Mixed $p$-spin spherical model Hamiltonian
nodes.statement: The Hamiltonian of the mixed $p$-spin spherical model is given by \begin{align} H_N({\vec{\sigma}})=\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p H_{N,p}({\vec{\sigma}}) \end{align} with coefficients $(\beta_p)$ that satisfy $\beta_p\geq 0$ and decrease fast enough, $\sum_{p\geq 1}2^p\beta_p^2<\infty.$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.definiendum: Hamiltonian of the mixed $p$-spin spherical model
nodes.statement_short: Mixed model Hamiltonian $H_N=\sum_p\beta_p H_{N,p}$ with nonnegative, fast-decaying coefficients.

nodes.name: Mixed p-spin Hamiltonian (1.2)
nodes.statement: H_N({\vec{\sigma}})=\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p H_{N,p}({\vec{\sigma}})
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.label: eq2

nodes.name: Overlap $R_{1,2}$ and mixture function $\xi$
nodes.statement: This technical assumption ensures that on $S_N$ the series $(\ref{eq2})$ converges a.s. and the covariance of the Gaussian process is given by a function of the normalized scalar product, called the overlap, $R_{1,2}=N^{-1}\sum_{i\leq N}\sigma_i^1\sigma_i^2$ of spin configurations ${\vec{\sigma}}^1$ and ${\vec{\sigma}}^2,$ $$ \mathbb{E}H_N({\vec{\sigma}}^1)H_N({\vec{\sigma}}^2)=N\xi(R_{1,2}), $$ where $\mathbb{E}$ is the expectation with respect to all Gaussian randomness and $\xi(x)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p^2 x^p.$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.statement_short: Covariance of $H_N$ is $N\xi(R_{1,2})$ where $R_{1,2}$ is the overlap and $\xi(x)=\sum_p\beta_p^2x^p$.

nodes.name: Parisi parameter sequences $\mathbf{m},\mathbf{q}$
nodes.statement: Given $k\geq 1$, let $\mathbf{m}=(m_\ell)_{0\leq \ell\leq k}$ and $\mathbf{q}=(q_\ell)_{0\leq \ell\leq k+1}$ be two sequences satisfying \begin{align*} &0=m_0\leq m_1\leq\ldots\leq m_{k-1}\leq m_k=1,\\ &0=q_0\leq q_1\leq \ldots \leq q_k\leq q_{k+1}=1. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.statement_short: Nondecreasing sequences $\mathbf m$ (from 0 to 1) and $\mathbf q$ (from 0 to 1) parametrizing the Parisi formula.

nodes.name: Distribution function $\vec{x}$ of a triplet
nodes.statement: One may think of the triplet $(k,\mathbf{m},\mathbf{q})$ as a distribution function $\vec{x}$ on $\left[0,1\right]$ with $\vec{x}(q)=m_\ell$ if $q_\ell\leq q<q_{\ell+1}$ for $0\leq \ell\leq k$ and $\vec{x}(1)=1.$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.

nodes.name: $d_\ell$
nodes.statement: We define for $1\leq \ell\leq k,$ $$d_\ell=\sum_{\ell\leq p\leq k}m_p(\xi'(q_{p+1})-\xi'(q_p)).$$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.

nodes.name: $D_\ell$
nodes.statement: For a given parameter $b>d_1,$ we define $D_\ell=b-d_\ell$ for $1\leq \ell\leq k$ and $D_{k+1}=b.$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.

nodes.name: $\theta(x)$
nodes.statement: Let $\theta(x)=x\xi'(x)-\xi(x).$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.

nodes.name: Parisi functional $\mathcal{P}$ (spherical form)
nodes.statement: The formulation of the Parisi formula involves a functional $\mathcal{P}$ of the distribution function $\vec{x}$, \begin{align*} \mathcal{P}(\vec{x})=\inf_{b>d_1}\frac{1}{2}\left(b-1-\log b+\frac{\xi'(q_1)}{D_1}+\sum_{1\leq \ell\leq k}\frac{1}{m_\ell}\log \frac{D_{\ell+1}}{D_\ell}-\sum_{1\leq \ell\leq k}m_\ell(\theta(q_{\ell+1})-\theta(q_{\ell}))\right), \end{align*} which is the limit of the Parisi functional described below.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.statement_short: Crisanti-Sommers type functional $\mathcal P(\vec x)$: infimum over $b>d_1$ of an explicit expression in $b,D_\ell,m_\ell,\xi,\theta$.

nodes.name: Gaussian vectors $\vec{z}_p$
nodes.statement: For every $M\geq 1,$ let $\vec{z}_p=(z_{p,1},\ldots,z_{p,M})$ for $0\leq p\leq k$ be centered Gaussian random vectors with $\mathbb{E}z_{p,i}z_{p,i'}=\delta_{i,i'}(\xi'(q_{p+1})-\xi'(q_p))$ for any $i\neq i'$ and let $(\vec{z}_p)_{0\leq p\leq k}$ be independent of each other.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.

nodes.name: Recursive quantities $X_p^M$
nodes.statement: Starting from \begin{align*} X_{k+1}^M=\log\int_{S_M}\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \left(\vec{z} _0+\cdots+\vec{z} _k\right)d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon}), \end{align*} we define decreasingly for $0\leq p\leq k,$ \begin{align*} X_p^M=\frac{1}{m_p}\log\mathbb{E}_p \exp m_p X_{p+1}^M, \end{align*} where $\mathbb{E}_p$ denotes the expectation in the random vectors $(\vec{z}_i)_{i\geq p}.$ When $m_p=0,$ this means $X_p^M=\mathbb{E}_p X_{p+1}^M.$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.statement_short: $X_{k+1}^M$ is a log-integral over $S_M$; $X_p^M$ defined backwards by $\frac1{m_p}\log\mathbb E_p\exp m_pX_{p+1}^M$.

nodes.name: Parisi functional $\mathcal{P}_M$
nodes.statement: Set the Parisi functional $$ \mathcal{P}_M(x)=X_0^M-\frac{1}{2}\sum_{1\leq p\leq k}m_p(\theta(q_{p+1})-\theta(q_p)). $$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.

nodes.name: Limit of the Parisi functionals
nodes.statement: A series of nontrivial applications of elementary large deviation principle implies $\mathcal{P}(\vec{x})=\lim_{M\rightarrow\infty}\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x})$ (see Proposition 3.1 \cite{Tal061}).
nodes.origin_citation: Talagrand 2006 (Free energy of the spherical mean field model), Proposition 3.1
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.statement_short: The finite-$M$ Parisi functionals $\mathcal P_M$ converge to $\mathcal P$ as $M\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Partition function $Z_N$
nodes.statement: Let us denote the partition function of the model by $$ Z_N=\int_{S_N}\exp H_N({\vec{\sigma}})d\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}}). $$
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.

nodes.name: The Parisi formula
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N=\inf_{\vec{x}}\mathcal{P}(\vec{x}), \end{align} where the infimum is taken over all possible choices of $\vec{x}$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
conclusions: where the infimum is taken over all possible choices of $\vec{x}$.
nodes.statement_short: The limiting free energy of the mixed $p$-spin spherical model equals the infimum of the Parisi functional $\mathcal P$.
nodes.label: thm1

nodes.name: Parisi formula identity (1.3)
nodes.statement: \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N=\inf_{\vec{x}}\mathcal{P}(\vec{x}),
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.
nodes.label: thm1:eq1

nodes.name: Free energy
nodes.statement: The quantity in the limit on the left-hand side of $(\ref{thm1:eq1})$ is usually called the free energy of this model and the formula on the right-hand side of $(\ref{thm1:eq1})$ is the famous Parisi formula in the spherical form, which is also known to have the Crisanti-Sommers representation \cite{CS92} (see Theorem 4.1 in \cite{Tal061}).
nodes.section: 1 Introduction and main results.

nodes.name: Cavity Gaussian fields $\vec z(\sigma)$ and $y(\sigma)$
nodes.statement: For $M,N\geq 1$, let us denote by $(\vec{z}({\vec{\sigma}})=(z_1({\vec{\sigma}}),\ldots,z_M({\vec{\sigma}})):{\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N)$ and $(y({\vec{\sigma}}):{\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N)$ two independent families of centered Gaussian random variables with covariances \begin{align} \begin{split} \mathbb{E}z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^1)z_{i'}({\vec{\sigma}}^2)&=\delta_{i,i'}\xi'(R_{1,2}) \end{split}\\ \begin{split} \mathbb{E}y({\vec{\sigma}}^1)y({\vec{\sigma}}^2)&=\theta(R_{1,2}) \end{split} \end{align} for every ${\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2\in S_N.$ These random variables are independent of all the other randomness.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Independent centered Gaussian fields on $S_N$ with covariances $\delta_{i,i'}\xi'(R_{1,2})$ and $\theta(R_{1,2})$.

nodes.name: Covariances of the cavity fields (2.1)-(2.2)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \mathbb{E}z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^1)z_{i'}({\vec{\sigma}}^2)&=\delta_{i,i'}\xi'(R_{1,2}) \end{split}\\ \begin{split} \mathbb{E}y({\vec{\sigma}}^1)y({\vec{\sigma}}^2)&=\theta(R_{1,2}) \end{split}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Gibbs measure $G_{M,N}$ of $H_{M,N}$
nodes.statement: Let $G_{M,N}$ be the Gibbs measure corresponding to the Hamiltonian \begin{align} H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}})&=\sum_{p\geq 1}\frac{\beta_p}{(M+N)^{(p-1)/2}}\sum_{1\leq i_1,\ldots,i_p\leq N}g_{i_1,\ldots,i_{p}}\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_p} \end{align} with reference measure $\lambda_N$ on $S_N$ and let $\left<\cdot\right>_{M,N}$ be the Gibbs average of $G_{M,N}.$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Hamiltonian $H_{M,N}$ (2.3)
nodes.statement: H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}})&=\sum_{p\geq 1}\frac{\beta_p}{(M+N)^{(p-1)/2}}\sum_{1\leq i_1,\ldots,i_p\leq N}g_{i_1,\ldots,i_{p}}\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_p}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.label: ASS:eq1

nodes.name: The A.S.S. scheme
nodes.statement: For any $\delta>0$ and $M\geq 1,$ the lower limit of $N^{-1}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N$ is bounded from below by \begin{align} \begin{split} &\frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\mathbb{E}\log \int_{S_M}\left<\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} ({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})- \mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}y({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}\right)\\ &\qquad\qquad -\delta\xi'(1)+\frac{1}{M}\log \nu_M(A_\delta), \end{split} \end{align} where $\nu_M$ is the probability measure of the $M$-dimensional Gaussian density and $$ A_\delta=\{\vec{\varepsilon}\in\mathbb{R}^M:M\leq\|\vec{\varepsilon}\|^2\leq M(1+\delta)\}. $$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
conclusions: the lower limit of $N^{-1}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N$ is bounded from below by
nodes.statement_short: Aizenman-Sims-Starr lower bound: the liminf free energy is at least a cavity functional of $G_{M,N}$ minus an error vanishing as $\delta\to0$, $M\to\infty$.
nodes.label: ASS:prop1

nodes.name: A.S.S. lower bound (2.4)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\mathbb{E}\log \int_{S_M}\left<\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} ({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})- \mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}y({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}\right)\\ &\qquad\qquad -\delta\xi'(1)+\frac{1}{M}\log \nu_M(A_\delta), \end{split}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Remarks on the A.S.S. scheme
nodes.statement: Note that a standard large deviation result yields $\lim_{M\rightarrow \infty}M^{-1}\log\nu_M(A_\delta)=0$ for every $\delta>0.$ Thus $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1})$ gives a lower bound for the lower limit of the free energy that will play an essential role in proving the Parisi formula in Section $\ref{proof}.$ Suppose that $\mu_N$ is the uniform probability measure on $\Sigma_N=\left\{-1,+1\right\}^N$. If we replace the measure space $(S_N,\lambda_N)$ by $(\Sigma_N,\mu_N)$ and ignore the error term $-\delta\xi'(1)+M^{-1}\log \nu_M(A_\delta)$ in $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1})$, then Theorem \ref{ASS:prop1} gives the A.S.S. scheme for the Ising spin glass model with general mixed $p$-spin interactions (see e.g. Section 15.8 \cite{Tal11}).
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: The error term vanishes as $M\to\infty$; replacing the sphere by the hypercube recovers the Ising A.S.S. scheme.

nodes.name: Poincaré's lemma
nodes.statement: To deal with this obstacle, we will use the idea of Poincar\'{e}'s lemma (see page 77 \cite{ST93}) that the projection on any fixed $M$ coordinates of the uniform probability measure $\lambda_{M+N}$ on the sphere $S_{M+N}$ converge weakly to $M$-dimensional standard Gaussian measure as $N$ tends to infinity.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
conclusions: the projection on any fixed $M$ coordinates of the uniform probability measure $\lambda_{M+N}$ on the sphere $S_{M+N}$ converge weakly to $M$-dimensional standard Gaussian measure as $N$ tends to infinity
nodes.statement_short: Projections of uniform measure on $S_{M+N}$ onto $M$ coordinates converge weakly to the standard Gaussian.

nodes.name: Cavity decomposition of $H_{M+N}$
nodes.statement: For ${\vec{\rho}}\in S_{M+N},$ let us write ${\vec{\rho}}=({\vec{\sigma}},\vec{\varepsilon})$ for the first $N$ coordinates ${\vec{\sigma}}=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_N)$ and the last $M$ cavity coordinates $\vec{\varepsilon}=(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_M)$ and write \begin{align*} H_{M+N}({\vec{\rho}})&=H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}})+\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i Z_i({\vec{\sigma}})+\gamma({\vec{\rho}}), \end{align*} where $H_{M,N}$ is given in $(\ref{ASS:eq1}),$ the term $\varepsilon_iZ_i({\vec{\sigma}})$ consists of all terms in $H_{M+N}$ with only one factor $\varepsilon_i$ from $\vec{\varepsilon}$ present, and the last term is the sum of terms with at least two factors in $\vec{\varepsilon}.$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\rho=(\sigma,\varepsilon)$ and write $H_{M+N}=H_{M,N}+\sum_i\varepsilon_iZ_i+\gamma$ by powers of cavity coordinates.

nodes.name: Normalized scalar product $R(\vec\omega,\vec\omega')$
nodes.statement: From now on, without causing any ambiguity, for any given vectors $\vec{\omega},\vec{\omega}'\in\Bbb{R}^K$ for some $K\geq 1$, we define $R(\vec{\omega},\vec{\omega}')=K^{-1}\sum_{i\leq K}\omega_i\omega_i'.$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Covariance structure of the cavity decomposition
nodes.statement: One can check easily that \begin{align} \begin{split} \mathbb{E}H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}^1)H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}^2)&=(M+N)\xi\left(\frac{N}{M+N}R({\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2)\right), \end{split}\\ \begin{split} \mathbb{E}Z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^1)Z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^2)&=\xi'\left(\frac{N}{M+N}R({\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2)\right), \end{split}\\ \begin{split} \mathbb{E}\gamma({\vec{\rho}})^2&\leq \frac{M^2}{M+N}\xi''(1). \end{split} \end{align}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Covariances of $H_{M,N}$ and $Z_i$ are $\xi$, $\xi'$ of a rescaled overlap; $\mathbb E\gamma^2=O(M^2/(M+N))$.

nodes.name: Covariance identities (2.5)-(2.7)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \mathbb{E}H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}^1)H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}^2)&=(M+N)\xi\left(\frac{N}{M+N}R({\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2)\right), \end{split}\\ \begin{split} \mathbb{E}Z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^1)Z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^2)&=\xi'\left(\frac{N}{M+N}R({\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2)\right), \end{split}\\ \begin{split} \mathbb{E}\gamma({\vec{\rho}})^2&\leq \frac{M^2}{M+N}\xi''(1). \end{split}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Elementary liminf fact for sequences
nodes.statement: Let us notice an elementary fact that for a real-valued sequence $(c_N)$, if $\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}c_N/N=r\in\mathbb{R},$ then $M^{-1}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}(c_{M+N}-c_N)\leq r$ for every $M\geq 1.$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Reduction to the cavity ratio (2.8)
nodes.statement: This implies \begin{align} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}\log Z_N}{N}\geq\frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{Z_N} \end{align} and thus to obtain Theorem $\ref{ASS:prop1}$, it suffices to prove that $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1})$ is the lower bound of the right-hand side of $(\ref{ASS:main:eq0})$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
conclusions: it suffices to prove that $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1})$ is the lower bound of the right-hand side of $(\ref{ASS:main:eq0})$
nodes.statement_short: Free energy liminf is at least $M^{-1}\liminf\mathbb E\log Z_{M+N}/Z_N$, reducing Theorem 2 to bounding this ratio.

nodes.name: Cavity lower bound (2.8)
nodes.statement: &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\mathbb{E}\log Z_N}{N}\geq\frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{Z_N}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.label: ASS:main:eq0

nodes.name: Three-term decomposition (2.9)
nodes.statement: Let us write $\mathbb{E}\log{Z_{M+N}}/{Z_N}$ as \begin{align} \begin{split} &\mathbb{E}\log \int_{A_\delta}\left< \exp\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z}({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}d\nu_M(\vec{\varepsilon})-\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{S_N}\exp H_Nd\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}})}{\int_{S_N}\exp H_{M,N}d\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}})}\\ &+\mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}J_{M,N}d\nu_M(\vec{\varepsilon})}, \end{split} \end{align} where \begin{align*} J_{M,N}(\vec{\varepsilon})&=\int_{S_N}\exp(H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}})+\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} ({\vec{\sigma}}))d\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}}),\quad\vec{\varepsilon}\in\mathbb{R}^M. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\mathbb E\log Z_{M+N}/Z_N$ into a cavity term, a Hamiltonian-ratio term and a decoupling term involving $J_{M,N}$.

nodes.name: Decomposition (2.9)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\mathbb{E}\log \int_{A_\delta}\left< \exp\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z}({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}d\nu_M(\vec{\varepsilon})-\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{S_N}\exp H_Nd\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}})}{\int_{S_N}\exp H_{M,N}d\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}})}\\ &+\mathbb{E}\log\frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}J_{M,N}d\nu_M(\vec{\varepsilon})}, \end{split}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (Gaussian vs spherical integral)
nodes.statement: For $\vec{z}\in\mathbb{R}^M,$ we have \begin{align} \int_{A_\delta}\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z} d\nu_M(\vec{\varepsilon})\geq \nu_M\left(A_\delta\right)\int_{S_M}\exp\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon}). \end{align}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian integral of $e^{\varepsilon\cdot z}$ over the shell $A_\delta$ dominates $\nu_M(A_\delta)$ times the spherical integral.
nodes.label: ASS:lem5

nodes.statement: \int_{A_\delta}\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z} d\nu_M(\vec{\varepsilon})\geq \nu_M\left(A_\delta\right)\int_{S_M}\exp\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon}).

nodes.label: ASS:lem5:eq1

u_M,$ there exists a probability measure $\gamma_M$ on $\mathbb{R}^+$ such that $
u_M$ is the image of $\gamma_M	imes \lambda_M$ under the map $(s,\vec{\varepsilon}) \mapsto s\vec{\varepsilon}.$ For $1\leq s\leq (1+\delta)^{1/2}$, using symmetry,  egin{align*} \int \exp s\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z} d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})&=\int \cosh(s\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z})d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})\ &\geq \int \cosh(\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z})d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})=\int \exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z} d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon}). \end{align*} Therefore, $(ef{ASS:lem5:eq1})$ holds by  egin{align*} \int_{A_\delta}\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z} d
u_M(\vec{\varepsilon})&=\int_{1}^{(1+\delta)^{1/2}}\int_{S_M}\exp s\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})d\gamma_M(s)\ &\geq\int_{1}^{(1+\delta)^{1/2}}\int_{S_M}\exp\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})d\gamma_M(s)\ &= \gamma_M(\{1\leq s\leq (1+\delta)^{1/2}\})\int_{S_M}\exp\vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon}). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Polar decomposition of $\nu_M$ and monotonicity of $\cosh$ in the radius.

nodes.name: Lower bound for the first term (2.11)
nodes.statement: From this lemma and Fubini's theorem, the first term in $(\ref{ASS:main:eq1})$ is bounded from below by \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}\left<\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z}({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})+\log \nu_M(A_\delta) \end{align}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 1 and Fubini, the cavity term is at least the spherical cavity functional plus $\log\nu_M(A_\delta)$.

nodes.statement: \mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}\left<\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z}({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})+\log \nu_M(A_\delta)
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.label: ASS:lem5.1:eq1

nodes.name: Lemma 2 (Hamiltonian ratio term)
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left|\mathbb{E}\log\frac{ \int_{S_N}\exp H_{N}({\vec{\sigma}})d\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}})}{\int_{S_N}\exp H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}})d\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}})} -\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp\sqrt{M}y({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}\right|=0. \end{align}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: The log-ratio of $H_N$ and $H_{M,N}$ partition functions is asymptotically $\mathbb E\log\langle\exp\sqrt M y\rangle_{M,N}$.
nodes.label: ASS:lem4

nodes.statement: \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left|\mathbb{E}\log\frac{ \int_{S_N}\exp H_{N}({\vec{\sigma}})d\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}})}{\int_{S_N}\exp H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}})d\lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}})} -\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp\sqrt{M}y({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}\right|=0.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.label: ASS:lem4:eq1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Suppose $(y'({\vec{\sigma}}):{\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N)$ is a family of centered Gaussian random variables independent of all the other randomness such that in distribution \begin{align*} H_N({\vec{\sigma}})=H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}})+\sqrt{M}y'({\vec{\sigma}}). \end{align*} It is easy to check that $\mathbb{E}y'({\vec{\sigma}}^1)y'({\vec{\sigma}}^2)=\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p^2D_pN^pR({\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2)^{p}$, where $$ D_{p}=\frac{1}{M}\left(\frac{1}{N^{p-1}}-\frac{1}{(M+N)^{p-1}}\right) $$ satisfies $N^pD_{p}\rightarrow p-1.$ Recall $y({\vec{\sigma}})$ from $(\ref{ASS:eq0.2}).$ Let us consider the interpolating free energy \begin{align*} \psi(t)&=\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}\left(\sqrt{t}y'({\vec{\sigma}})+\sqrt{1-t}{y}({\vec{\sigma}})\right)\right>_{M,N}. \end{align*} Then $|\psi(1)-\psi(0)|$ gives the quantity in the limit on the left-hand side of $(\ref{ASS:lem4:eq1})$. Thus it suffices to prove that $\psi'(t)\rightarrow 0$ uniformly in $t\in (0,1)$ as $N\rightarrow\infty,$ which can be easily verified by using Gaussian integration by parts, as $N\rightarrow\infty,$ \begin{align*} \sup_{0<t<1}|\psi'(t)|&\leq M\sup_{{\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2\in S_N}|\mathbb{E}y'({\vec{\sigma}}^1)y'({\vec{\sigma}}^2)-\mathbb{E}y({\vec{\sigma}}^1)y({\vec{\sigma}}^2)|\\ &=M\sup_{{\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2\in S_N}\left|\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p^2(D_{p}N^p-(p-1))R({\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2)^p\right|\rightarrow 0. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian interpolation between $y'$ and $y$; the derivative vanishes uniformly by Gaussian integration by parts.

nodes.name: Unit sphere $S_K^1$ and its area
nodes.statement: For $K\geq 1,$ we denote by $S_K^1$ the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^K$ and by $|S_K^1|$ the area of $S_K^1$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: $A_{M,N}$ and $b_{M,N}$
nodes.statement: Set \begin{align*} A_{M,N}&=\prod_{j=1}^M\left[-\sqrt{M+N+1-j},\sqrt{M+N+1-j}\right],\\ b_{M,N}&=\prod_{j=1}^M\frac{|S_{M+N-j}^1|}{|S_{M+N+1-j}^1|\sqrt{M+N+1-j}}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Densities $F_{M,N}$ and $F_M$
nodes.statement: Define \begin{align*} F_{M,N}(\vec{\varepsilon})&=b_{M,N}\prod_{j=1}^M\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon_j^2}{M+N+1-j}\right)^{\frac{M+N-j-2}{2}},\quad\vec{\varepsilon}\in A_{M,N},\\ F_M(\vec{\varepsilon})&=\left(\frac{1}{2\pi}\right)^{M/2}\exp\left(-\frac{\|\vec{\varepsilon}\|^2}{2}\right),\quad\vec{\varepsilon}\in \mathbb{R}^M. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: $F_{M,N}$: density of $M$ cavity coordinates under uniform measure on $S_{M+N}$; $F_M$: standard Gaussian density.

nodes.name: Rescaling factors $a_\ell$
nodes.statement: Define $a_1=1$ and for $2\leq \ell\leq M+1,$ $$ a_\ell(\vec{\varepsilon})=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell-1}\sqrt{1+\frac{1-\varepsilon_j^2}{M+N-j}},\quad \vec{\varepsilon}\in A_{M,N}. $$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Lemma 3 (decoupling of the spherical measure)
nodes.statement: Suppose that $f$ is a nonnegative function defined on $S_{M+N}.$ Then we have \begin{align} \int_{S_{M+N}}f({\vec{\rho}})d\lambda_{M+N}({\vec{\rho}}) &=\int_{A_{M,N}} F_{M,N}(\vec{\varepsilon})d\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}\int_{S_N}f\left({\vec{\sigma}} a_{M+1},\varepsilon_{1}a_{1},\ldots,\varepsilon_Ma_M\right)d\lambda_{N}({\vec{\sigma}}). \end{align}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
assumptions: Suppose that $f$ is a nonnegative function defined on $S_{M+N}.$
nodes.statement_short: Integration over $S_{M+N}$ factors into an integral over $M$ cavity coordinates with density $F_{M,N}$ and a rescaled integral over $S_N$.
nodes.label: ASS:lem1

nodes.statement: \int_{S_{M+N}}f({\vec{\rho}})d\lambda_{M+N}({\vec{\rho}}) &=\int_{A_{M,N}} F_{M,N}(\vec{\varepsilon})d\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}\int_{S_N}f\left({\vec{\sigma}} a_{M+1},\varepsilon_{1}a_{1},\ldots,\varepsilon_Ma_M\right)d\lambda_{N}({\vec{\sigma}}).
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.label: ASS:lem1:eq1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: This is an elementary calculus formula that follows by an induction argument starting from \begin{align*} \int_{S_K}f({\vec{\rho}})d\lambda_K({\vec{\rho}})&=\frac{|S_{K-1}^1|}{|S_K^1|\sqrt{K}}\int_{-\sqrt{K}}^{\sqrt{K}}\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon^2}{K}\right)^{\frac{K-3}{2}}d\varepsilon \int_{S_{K-1}}f\left({\vec{\sigma}} \sqrt{\frac{K-\varepsilon^2}{K-1}},\varepsilon\right)d\lambda_{K-1}({\vec{\sigma}}) \end{align*} for every $K\geq 2.$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the number of peeled coordinates using the one-coordinate disintegration formula on $S_K$.

nodes.name: Cavity coordinates are asymptotically Gaussian
nodes.statement: As an immediate consequence of Lemma \ref{ASS:lem1}, the cavity coordinates converge weakly to the $M$-dimensional standard Gaussian random vector as $N$ tends to infinity.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.name: Decomposition of the decoupling term (2.14)
nodes.statement: We write $\mathbb{E}\log {Z_{M+N}}/{\int_{A_\delta}J_{M,N}d\nu_M(\vec{\varepsilon})}$ as \begin{align} &\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}+\mathbb{E}\log \frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}. \end{align}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.

nodes.statement: &\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}+\mathbb{E}\log \frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.label: sec2:eq1

nodes.name: Lemma 4
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}} \geq -M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Replacing $Z_{M+N}$ by the decoupled integral with density $F_{M,N}$ costs at most $M\delta\xi'(1)$.
nodes.label: ASS:lem2

nodes.statement: &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}} \geq -M\delta\xi'(1).
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.label: ASS:lem2:eq1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Suppose that $(H_{M,N}'({\vec{\sigma}}):{\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N)$ is an independent copy of $(H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}):{\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N)$ and is independent of all the other randomness. We consider the following interpolating Hamiltonian \begin{align*} \varphi(t)=&\mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}(\vec{\varepsilon})d\vec{\varepsilon}\int_{S_N}\exp(H_{1,t}({\vec{\rho}})+H_{2,t}({\vec{\rho}})+H_{3,t}({\vec{\rho}}))d \lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}}), \end{align*} where for ${\vec{\rho}}=({\vec{\sigma}},\vec{\varepsilon})$ with ${\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N$ and $\vec{\varepsilon}\in A_\delta,$ \begin{align*} H_{1,t}({\vec{\rho}})&=\sqrt{t}H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}} a_{M+1})+\sqrt{1-t}H_{M,N}'({\vec{\sigma}})\\ H_{2,t}({\vec{\rho}})&=\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i\left(\sqrt{t}a_i Z_i({\vec{\sigma}} a_{M+1})+\sqrt{1-t}z_i({\vec{\sigma}})\right)\\ H_{3,t}({\vec{\rho}})&=\sqrt{t}\gamma({\vec{\sigma}} a_{M+1},\varepsilon_1a_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_Ma_M). \end{align*} From $(\ref{ASS:lem1:eq1})$, obviously $\varphi(1)\leq\mathbb{E}\log Z_{M+N}$ when $N$ is large enough. On the other hand, using Gaussian integration by parts and replicas ${\vec{\rho}}^1=({\vec{\sigma}}^1,\vec{\varepsilon}^1)$ and ${\vec{\rho}}^2=({\vec{\sigma}}^2,\vec{\varepsilon}^2),$ it follows that \begin{align*} \varphi'(t)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j\leq 3}\left(\mathbb{E}\left<U_{j}({\vec{\rho}},{\vec{\rho}})\right>_t-\mathbb{E}\left<U_j({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)\right>_t\right), \end{align*} where $\left<\cdot\right>_t$ is the Gibbs average corresponding to random weights $F_{M,N}\exp(H_{1,t}+H_{2,t}+H_{3,t})$ with reference measure $\lambda_N\times d\vec{\varepsilon}$ on $S_N\times A_\delta$ and \begin{align*} U_1({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)&=\mathbb{E}H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}^1a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^1))H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}^2a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2))- \mathbb{E}H_{M,N}'({\vec{\sigma}}^1)H_{M,N}'({\vec{\sigma}}^2)\\ U_2({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)&=\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i^1\varepsilon_i^2\left(a_i(\vec{\varepsilon}^1)a_{i}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2)\mathbb{E}Z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^1a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^1))Z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^2a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2)) -\mathbb{E}z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^1)z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^2)\right)\\ U_3({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)&=\mathbb{E}\gamma({\vec{\sigma}}^1a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^1),{\varepsilon}_1^1a_1(\vec{\varepsilon}^1),\ldots,{\varepsilon}_M^1a_M(\vec{\varepsilon}^1))\\ &\qquad\cdot\gamma({\vec{\sigma}}^2a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2),{\varepsilon}_1^2a_1(\vec{\varepsilon}^2),\ldots,{\varepsilon}_M^2a_M(\vec{\varepsilon}^2)). \end{align*} From $(\ref{ASS:eq0.1})$, $(\ref{ASS:eq2.2}),$ and $(\ref{ASS:eq2.3})$, it is easy to see that for $j=2,3,$ $$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{{\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2\in S_N\times A_\delta}|U_j({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)|\rightarrow 0$$ and from $(\ref{ASS:eq2.1})$ and using mean value theorem, \begin{align*} &\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{{\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2\in S_N\times A_\delta}|U_1({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)|\\ &\leq \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\xi'(1)(M+N)\sup_{\vec{\varepsilon}^1,\vec{\varepsilon}^2\in A_\delta}\left|\frac{N}{M+N}a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^1)a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2)-1\right|\\ &=\xi'(1)\sup_{\vec{\varepsilon}^1,\vec{\varepsilon}^2\in A_\delta}\left|M-\frac{\|\vec{\varepsilon}^1\|^2+\|\vec{\varepsilon}^2\|^2}{2}\right|\leq M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align*} Thus we conclude that $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{0<t<1}|\varphi'(t)|\leq M\delta\xi'(1)$ and so $(\ref{ASS:lem2:eq1})$ follows by \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}&\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}(\varphi(1)-\varphi(0))\\ &\geq -\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{0<t<1}|\varphi'(t)|\geq -M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian interpolation between the exact cavity Hamiltonian and the decoupled one; bound the derivative uniformly. The key estimate uses the mean value theorem on $\|\varepsilon\|^2\in[M,M(1+\delta)]$.

nodes.name: Lemma 5
nodes.statement: We have \begin{align} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}\geq 0. \end{align}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Swapping the finite-$N$ cavity density $F_{M,N}$ for the Gaussian density $F_M$ does not decrease the limit.
nodes.label: ASS:lem3

nodes.statement: \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}\geq 0.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.label: ASS:lem3:eq1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Using the inequality $\log(1-x)\geq -2x$ for $0<x<1/2,$ when $N$ is sufficiently large, we have for every $\vec{\varepsilon}\in A_\delta,$ \begin{align*} &\log \frac{F_{M,N}(\vec{\varepsilon})}{F_M(\vec{\varepsilon})}\\ &=\log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log\frac{1}{2\pi}+\sum_{j=1}^M\frac{M+N-j-2}{2}\log\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon_j^2}{M+N+1-j}\right)+\frac{\|\vec{\varepsilon}\|^2}{2}\\ &\geq \log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log\frac{1}{2\pi}+\frac{3\|\vec{\varepsilon}\|^2}{M+N}. \end{align*} Note that $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}b_{M,N}=1/(2\pi)^{M/2}$ as can be seen from $(\ref{ASS:lem1:eq1})$ with $f=1.$ By Jensen's inequality, we obtain \begin{align*} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}\exp \left(\log F_{M,N}/F_{M}\right)d\vec{\varepsilon}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}\\ &\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}\log F_{M,N}/F_{M}d\vec{\varepsilon}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}\\ &\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log \frac{1}{2\pi}+\frac{3M}{M+N}\right)=0 \end{align*} and this gives $(\ref{ASS:lem3:eq1}).$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise lower bound on $\log F_{M,N}/F_M$ via $\log(1-x)\ge-2x$, then Jensen's inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: \noindent{\bf Proof of Theorem \ref{ASS:prop1}.} From $(\ref{ASS:main:eq0})$, $(\ref{ASS:main:eq1})$, and $(\ref{sec2:eq1}),$ using Lemmas $\ref{ASS:lem4},$ $\ref{ASS:lem2}$, and $\ref{ASS:lem3},$ the lower limit of $N^{-1}{\mathbb{E}\log Z_{N}}$ is bounded from below by \begin{align*} \frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}\left<\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot\vec{z}({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}d\nu_M(\vec{\varepsilon})-\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp\sqrt{M}y({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}\right)-\delta\xi'(1) \end{align*} and then $(\ref{ASS:lem5.1:eq1})$ yields $(\ref{ASS:prop1:eq1}).$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the reduction (2.8), decompositions (2.9), (2.14) and Lemmas 2, 4, 5, then Lemma 1's bound (2.11).

nodes.name: Guerra's replica symmetry breaking bound (spherical, even p)
nodes.statement: In the case when $p$-spin interactions for odd $p\geq 3$ are not present in $(\ref{eq2})$, this scheme implies that the upper limit of the free energy is bounded from above by $\inf_{\vec{x}}\mathcal{P}(\vec{x}).$
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
assumptions: In the case when $p$-spin interactions for odd $p\geq 3$ are not present in $(\ref{eq2})$,
conclusions: the upper limit of the free energy is bounded from above by $\inf_{\vec{x}}\mathcal{P}(\vec{x}).$

nodes.name: Upper bound for general mixed p-spin via positivity principle
nodes.statement: The fact that this bound still holds in the general mixed $p$-spin case relies on Talagrand's positivity principle on the overlap (see \cite{Tal03} and Section 12.3 in \cite{Tal11}) that is deduced from the validity of the G.G. identities \cite{GG98} derived by a perturbation trick on the Hamiltonian.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Guerra's upper bound extends to general mixtures using Talagrand's positivity principle from the Ghirlanda-Guerra identities.

nodes.name: Perturbation Hamiltonian $H_N^{pert}$
nodes.statement: For each $u=(u_p)_{p\geq 1}$ with $1\leq u_p\leq 2,$ let us consider a perturbation Hamiltonian \begin{align*} H_{N}^{pert}({\vec{\sigma}})=\frac{1}{N^{1/8}}\sum_{p\geq 1}\frac{u_p}{2^p}H_{N,p}'({\vec{\sigma}}), \end{align*} where $H_{N,p}'({\vec{\sigma}})$ are independent copies of the $p$-spin Hamiltonian in $(\ref{eq1})$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.

nodes.name: Perturbation does not affect the limit
nodes.statement: Since the perturbation term is of a small order, replacing $H_N$ with $H_N+H_N^{pert}$ in $(\ref{thm1:eq1})$ obviously does not affect the limit and in addition, the following A.S.S. scheme also holds.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.

nodes.name: Perturbation Hamiltonian $H_{M,N}^{pert}$
nodes.statement: Consider another perturbation Hamiltonian \begin{align*} H_{M,N}^{pert}({\vec{\sigma}})=\frac{1}{(M+N)^{1/8}}\sum_{p\geq 1}\frac{u_p}{2^p}\left(\frac{N}{M+N}\right)^{(p-1)/2}H_{N,p}'({\vec{\sigma}}). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.

nodes.name: Perturbed Gibbs measure $G_{M,N}^-$
nodes.statement: Let $G_{M,N}^-$ be the Gibbs measure corresponding to the Hamiltonian $H_{M,N}+H_{M,N}^{pert}$ with reference measure $\lambda_N$ and $\left<\cdot\right>_{M,N}^-$ be the average with respect to the product Gibbs measure $G_{M,N}^{-\otimes\infty}.$
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.

nodes.name: The A.S.S. scheme (perturbed Hamiltonian)
nodes.statement: Recall $A_\delta$ and $\nu_M$ from Theorem $\ref{ASS:prop1}.$ For every $\delta>0$ and $M\geq 1,$ we have \begin{align} \begin{split} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N\\ &\geq\frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{u}\left(\mathbb{E}\log \int_{S_M}\left<\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} ({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}^-d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})- \mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}y({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}^-\right)\\ &\qquad\qquad -\delta\xi'(1)+\frac{1}{M}\log \nu_M(A_\delta), \end{split} \end{align} where the supremum is taken over all $u=(u_{p})_{p\geq 1}$ with $1\leq u_p\leq 2.$
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: The A.S.S. lower bound holds for the perturbed Hamiltonians, uniformly with a supremum over perturbation parameters $u$.
nodes.label: ASS:cor

nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N\\ &\geq\frac{1}{M}\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{u}\left(\mathbb{E}\log \int_{S_M}\left<\exp \vec{\varepsilon}\cdot \vec{z} ({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}^-d\lambda_M(\vec{\varepsilon})- \mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}y({\vec{\sigma}})\right>_{M,N}^-\right)\\ &\qquad\qquad -\delta\xi'(1)+\frac{1}{M}\log \nu_M(A_\delta), \end{split}
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1 (sketch)
nodes.statement: Starting with the Hamiltonian $H_{M+N}+H_{M+N}^{pert}$ and using the fact that $H_{M+N}^{pert}$ is of a small order, one may easily find that the same arguments in the proof of Theorem $\ref{ASS:prop1}$ also work in Proposition $\ref{ASS:cor}$, so we will leave this part of the proof to the readers.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Same argument as Theorem 2, the perturbation being of small order.

nodes.name: Overlap matrix $R^{M,N}$
nodes.statement: Let $({\vec{\sigma}}^\ell)_{\ell\geq 1}$ be an i.i.d. sample from $G_{M,N}^-$ and let $R^{M,N}=(R_{\ell,\ell'}^{M,N})_{\ell,\ell'\geq 1}$ be the normalized Gram matrix, or matrix of overlaps, of this sample.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.

nodes.name: Index set $\mathcal{C}$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the collection of all $(p,n,f)$ with $p\geq 1,$ $n\geq 2,$ and $f$ being a monomial of $(R_{\ell,\ell'}^{M,N})_{\ell,\ell'\leq n}.$
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.

nodes.name: G.G. defect $\Phi_{M,N}(p,n,f)$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (lower bound)
nodes.statement: \noindent{\bf Proof of Theorem \ref{thm1}.} If we denote by $\vec{x}^M$ the distribution of $R_{1,2}^M,$ it follows that by using $(\ref{AGMU:add1})$ and $(\ref{AGM:eq6})$, \begin{align} \Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)=\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}^M). \end{align} From Helly's selection theorem, $(\vec{x}^M)_{M\geq 1}$ contains a weakly convergent subsequence with limit $\vec{x}^\infty.$ For clarity, we simply use $(\vec{x}^M)$ to denote this subsequence. Using $(\ref{AGM:prop2})$ and $(\ref{AGM:eq7})$, if we set $\vec{x}_k^\infty=H_k(\vec{x}^\infty),$ then \begin{align*} \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}_k^{\infty})\right| &=\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}_k^{\infty})\right|\\ &\leq \frac{\xi'(1)}{2}\left(\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}d(\vec{x}^M,\vec{x}^{\infty})+d(\vec{x}^\infty,\vec{x}_k^{\infty})\right)\\ &=\frac{\xi'(1)}{2}d(\vec{x}^\infty,\vec{x}_k^{\infty}) \end{align*} for every $k\geq 1.$ To sum up, from $(\ref{AGM:eq2.1}),$ $(\ref{AGM:eq8})$, and this inequality, we conclude that \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N&\geq \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left( \Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)+\frac{1}{M}\log\nu_M(A_\delta)\right)-\delta\xi'(1)\\ &\geq \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}_k^\infty)-\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}_k^\infty)\right|-\delta\xi'(1)\\ &\geq\inf_{\vec{x}}\mathcal{P}(\vec{x})-\frac{\xi'(1)}{2}d(\vec{x}^\infty,\vec{x}_k^{\infty})-\delta\xi'(1) \end{align*} for every $k\geq 1$ and $\delta>0$ and this completes our proof by letting $\delta\rightarrow 0$ and $k\rightarrow\infty.$

nodes.statement: Recall $y({\vec{\sigma}})$ from $(\ref{ASS:eq0.2}).$ Let us consider the interpolating free energy \begin{align*} \psi(t)&=\mathbb{E}\log \left<\exp \sqrt{M}\left(\sqrt{t}y'({\vec{\sigma}})+\sqrt{1-t}{y}({\vec{\sigma}})\right)\right>_{M,N}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Define interpolating free energy $\psi(t)$ between $y'$ and $y$

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: Then $|\psi(1)-\psi(0)|$ gives the quantity in the limit on the left-hand side of $(\ref{ASS:lem4:eq1})$.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce the lemma to $\psi(1)-\psi(0)\to0$

nodes.name: Derivative bound
nodes.statement: Thus it suffices to prove that $\psi'(t)\rightarrow 0$ uniformly in $t\in (0,1)$ as $N\rightarrow\infty,$ which can be easily verified by using Gaussian integration by parts, as $N\rightarrow\infty,$ \begin{align*} \sup_{0<t<1}|\psi'(t)|&\leq M\sup_{{\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2\in S_N}|\mathbb{E}y'({\vec{\sigma}}^1)y'({\vec{\sigma}}^2)-\mathbb{E}y({\vec{\sigma}}^1)y({\vec{\sigma}}^2)|\\ &=M\sup_{{\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2\in S_N}\left|\sum_{p\geq 1}\beta_p^2(D_{p}N^p-(p-1))R({\vec{\sigma}}^1,{\vec{\sigma}}^2)^p\right|\rightarrow 0. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian integration by parts bounds $\psi'$ by covariance differences, which vanish

nodes.name: Interpolation $\varphi(t)$
nodes.statement: Suppose that $(H_{M,N}'({\vec{\sigma}}):{\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N)$ is an independent copy of $(H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}):{\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N)$ and is independent of all the other randomness. We consider the following interpolating Hamiltonian \begin{align*} \varphi(t)=&\mathbb{E}\log\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}(\vec{\varepsilon})d\vec{\varepsilon}\int_{S_N}\exp(H_{1,t}({\vec{\rho}})+H_{2,t}({\vec{\rho}})+H_{3,t}({\vec{\rho}}))d \lambda_N({\vec{\sigma}}), \end{align*} where for ${\vec{\rho}}=({\vec{\sigma}},\vec{\varepsilon})$ with ${\vec{\sigma}}\in S_N$ and $\vec{\varepsilon}\in A_\delta,$ \begin{align*} H_{1,t}({\vec{\rho}})&=\sqrt{t}H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}} a_{M+1})+\sqrt{1-t}H_{M,N}'({\vec{\sigma}})\\ H_{2,t}({\vec{\rho}})&=\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i\left(\sqrt{t}a_i Z_i({\vec{\sigma}} a_{M+1})+\sqrt{1-t}z_i({\vec{\sigma}})\right)\\ H_{3,t}({\vec{\rho}})&=\sqrt{t}\gamma({\vec{\sigma}} a_{M+1},\varepsilon_1a_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_Ma_M). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Define interpolation $\varphi(t)$ between exact and decoupled cavity Hamiltonians

nodes.name: Endpoint $t=1$
nodes.statement: From $(\ref{ASS:lem1:eq1})$, obviously $\varphi(1)\leq\mathbb{E}\log Z_{M+N}$ when $N$ is large enough.
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3 gives $\varphi(1)\le\mathbb E\log Z_{M+N}$

nodes.name: Derivative formula
nodes.statement: On the other hand, using Gaussian integration by parts and replicas ${\vec{\rho}}^1=({\vec{\sigma}}^1,\vec{\varepsilon}^1)$ and ${\vec{\rho}}^2=({\vec{\sigma}}^2,\vec{\varepsilon}^2),$ it follows that \begin{align*} \varphi'(t)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{j\leq 3}\left(\mathbb{E}\left<U_{j}({\vec{\rho}},{\vec{\rho}})\right>_t-\mathbb{E}\left<U_j({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)\right>_t\right), \end{align*} where $\left<\cdot\right>_t$ is the Gibbs average corresponding to random weights $F_{M,N}\exp(H_{1,t}+H_{2,t}+H_{3,t})$ with reference measure $\lambda_N\times d\vec{\varepsilon}$ on $S_N\times A_\delta$ and \begin{align*} U_1({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)&=\mathbb{E}H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}^1a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^1))H_{M,N}({\vec{\sigma}}^2a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2))- \mathbb{E}H_{M,N}'({\vec{\sigma}}^1)H_{M,N}'({\vec{\sigma}}^2)\\ U_2({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)&=\sum_{i\leq M}\varepsilon_i^1\varepsilon_i^2\left(a_i(\vec{\varepsilon}^1)a_{i}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2)\mathbb{E}Z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^1a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^1))Z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^2a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2)) -\mathbb{E}z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^1)z_i({\vec{\sigma}}^2)\right)\\ U_3({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)&=\mathbb{E}\gamma({\vec{\sigma}}^1a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^1),{\varepsilon}_1^1a_1(\vec{\varepsilon}^1),\ldots,{\varepsilon}_M^1a_M(\vec{\varepsilon}^1))\\ &\qquad\cdot\gamma({\vec{\sigma}}^2a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2),{\varepsilon}_1^2a_1(\vec{\varepsilon}^2),\ldots,{\varepsilon}_M^2a_M(\vec{\varepsilon}^2)). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian integration by parts expresses $\varphi'$ via covariance differences $U_j$

nodes.name: Bound $U_j$
nodes.statement: From $(\ref{ASS:eq0.1})$, $(\ref{ASS:eq2.2}),$ and $(\ref{ASS:eq2.3})$, it is easy to see that for $j=2,3,$ $$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{{\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2\in S_N\times A_\delta}|U_j({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)|\rightarrow 0$$ and from $(\ref{ASS:eq2.1})$ and using mean value theorem, \begin{align*} &\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{{\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2\in S_N\times A_\delta}|U_1({\vec{\rho}}^1,{\vec{\rho}}^2)|\\ &\leq \lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\xi'(1)(M+N)\sup_{\vec{\varepsilon}^1,\vec{\varepsilon}^2\in A_\delta}\left|\frac{N}{M+N}a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^1)a_{M+1}(\vec{\varepsilon}^2)-1\right|\\ &=\xi'(1)\sup_{\vec{\varepsilon}^1,\vec{\varepsilon}^2\in A_\delta}\left|M-\frac{\|\vec{\varepsilon}^1\|^2+\|\vec{\varepsilon}^2\|^2}{2}\right|\leq M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: $U_2,U_3\to0$; $U_1$ bounded by $M\delta\xi'(1)$ by the mean value theorem

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus we conclude that $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{0<t<1}|\varphi'(t)|\leq M\delta\xi'(1)$ and so $(\ref{ASS:lem2:eq1})$ follows by \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log \frac{Z_{M+N}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_{M,N}J_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}&\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}(\varphi(1)-\varphi(0))\\ &\geq -\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\sup_{0<t<1}|\varphi'(t)|\geq -M\delta\xi'(1). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the derivative bound over $t$

nodes.name: Pointwise bound
nodes.statement: Using the inequality $\log(1-x)\geq -2x$ for $0<x<1/2,$ when $N$ is sufficiently large, we have for every $\vec{\varepsilon}\in A_\delta,$ \begin{align*} &\log \frac{F_{M,N}(\vec{\varepsilon})}{F_M(\vec{\varepsilon})}\\ &=\log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log\frac{1}{2\pi}+\sum_{j=1}^M\frac{M+N-j-2}{2}\log\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon_j^2}{M+N+1-j}\right)+\frac{\|\vec{\varepsilon}\|^2}{2}\\ &\geq \log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log\frac{1}{2\pi}+\frac{3\|\vec{\varepsilon}\|^2}{M+N}. \end{align*}
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise lower bound on $\log F_{M,N}/F_M$ on $A_\delta$

nodes.name: Limit of $b_{M,N}$
nodes.statement: Note that $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}b_{M,N}=1/(2\pi)^{M/2}$ as can be seen from $(\ref{ASS:lem1:eq1})$ with $f=1.$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3 with $f=1$ gives the limit of $b_{M,N}$

nodes.name: Jensen
nodes.statement: By Jensen's inequality, we obtain \begin{align*} &\liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\log\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}\exp \left(\log F_{M,N}/F_{M}\right)d\vec{\varepsilon}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}\\ &\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}\frac{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}\log F_{M,N}/F_{M}d\vec{\varepsilon}}{\int_{A_\delta}F_MJ_{M,N}d\vec{\varepsilon}}\\ &\geq \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\left(\log b_{M,N}-\frac{M}{2}\log \frac{1}{2\pi}+\frac{3M}{M+N}\right)=0 \end{align*} and this gives $(\ref{ASS:lem3:eq1}).$
nodes.section: 2 The A.S.S. scheme for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality and the pointwise bound give the claim

nodes.name: Chebyshev
nodes.statement: By Chebyshev's inequality, $\mathbb{P}_u(\Phi_{M,N}\leq \eta)\geq 1-\mathbb{E}_u\Phi_{M,N}/\eta$ for every $\eta>0.$
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Chebyshev bound on $\Phi_{M,N}$

nodes.name: Choose $u^{M,N}$
nodes.statement: If we pick $\eta=2\mathbb{E}_u\Phi_{M,N},$ it implies that for any $M$ and $N$ we can always find $u^{M,N}=(u_p^{M,N})_{p\geq 1}$ such that $\Phi_{M,N}(u^{M,N})\leq 2\mathbb{E}_u\Phi_{M,N}$.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Select $u^{M,N}$ with defect at most twice its mean

nodes.name: Mean defect vanishes
nodes.statement: Note that using $\Phi_{M,N}(n,p,f)\leq 2$ and the G.G. identities $(\ref{prop:GG:eq1})$ implies $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\mathbb{E}_u\Phi_{M,N}=0.$
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Mean defect vanishes by the G.G. identities

nodes.name: Identify $\Psi_M$
nodes.statement: If we denote by $\vec{x}^M$ the distribution of $R_{1,2}^M,$ it follows that by using $(\ref{AGMU:add1})$ and $(\ref{AGM:eq6})$, \begin{align} \Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)=\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}^M). \end{align}
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Pass $k\to\infty$ in (3.7)-(3.8) to get $\Psi_M(\mathcal L^M)=\mathcal P_M(\vec x^M)$

nodes.name: Helly selection
nodes.statement: From Helly's selection theorem, $(\vec{x}^M)_{M\geq 1}$ contains a weakly convergent subsequence with limit $\vec{x}^\infty.$ For clarity, we simply use $(\vec{x}^M)$ to denote this subsequence.
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Extract a weakly convergent subsequence $\vec x^M\to\vec x^\infty$

nodes.name: Lipschitz comparison
nodes.statement: Using $(\ref{AGM:prop2})$ and $(\ref{AGM:eq7})$, if we set $\vec{x}_k^\infty=H_k(\vec{x}^\infty),$ then \begin{align*} \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}_k^{\infty})\right| &=\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}_k^{\infty})\right|\\ &\leq \frac{\xi'(1)}{2}\left(\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}d(\vec{x}^M,\vec{x}^{\infty})+d(\vec{x}^\infty,\vec{x}_k^{\infty})\right)\\ &=\frac{\xi'(1)}{2}d(\vec{x}^\infty,\vec{x}_k^{\infty}) \end{align*} for every $k\geq 1.$
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz bound compares $\Psi_M(\mathcal L^M)$ with $\mathcal P_M(\vec x_k^\infty)$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: To sum up, from $(\ref{AGM:eq2.1}),$ $(\ref{AGM:eq8})$, and this inequality, we conclude that \begin{align*} \liminf_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{N}\mathbb{E}\log Z_N&\geq \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left( \Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)+\frac{1}{M}\log\nu_M(A_\delta)\right)-\delta\xi'(1)\\ &\geq \limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}_k^\infty)-\limsup_{M\rightarrow\infty}\left|\Psi_M(\mathcal{L}^M)-\mathcal{P}_M(\vec{x}_k^\infty)\right|-\delta\xi'(1)\\ &\geq\inf_{\vec{x}}\mathcal{P}(\vec{x})-\frac{\xi'(1)}{2}d(\vec{x}^\infty,\vec{x}_k^{\infty})-\delta\xi'(1) \end{align*} for every $k\geq 1$ and $\delta>0$ and this completes our proof by letting $\delta\rightarrow 0$ and $k\rightarrow\infty.$
nodes.section: 3 Proof of the Parisi formula for spherical models.
nodes.statement_short: Combine with the A.S.S. bound and let $\delta\to0$, $k\to\infty$
